**Finding: deviation (LOL-CAP)**

The caps themselves are fine: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 mirror each other (greater of $100,000 or 12 months' charges paid), and Section 10's mutual consequential-damages exclusion expressly preserves Customer's payment obligations — all consistent with the playbook.

What fails the fallback is the carve-out set. Only indemnification payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the caps. There is nothing for breach of confidentiality, data protection or security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement — and the position is worse than neutral for us because (i) Section 6.0 makes Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the AECI for confidential information in the hosting environment, and (ii) Subsection 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data entirely.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a single new Section 9.3 carve-out provision inserted after 9.2, leaving the existing cap amounts and mutual structure untouched.
